omar: Heads up — after the tokenizer v2 rollout we saw a ~15% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for the mid-tail workload (p95 latency +120ms on average). suspecting key canonicalization differences + tool metadata ordering. anyone else seeing this?
jia: saw the same in profiler. kv_cache.lookup shows lots of misses where the only diff is JSON ordering in `tool_args` and a trailing space in system prompt. attaching a quick sample:```miss key A: "system:You are helpful"\nmiss key B: "system: You are helpful"```
kendra: oof. this sounds like both whitespace normalization and stable serialization for tool/function fields. we should avoid ad-hoc string concat as signature. recommend: (1) normalize system prompt whitespace, (2) stable-serialize tool metadata (sorted keys), (3) include tokenizer version in signature. low-risk hotfix: canonicalize prompt whitespace before hashing.
michael: quick numbers from my run: baseline hit-rate=78.2%, post-rollout=63.1%. warmup prefills recover ~6-7% but not enough. if we add tokenizer pin + stable-serialize, models jump back to ~76%.
natasha: note: batching heuristics also changed in the same release — the continuous-batcher now groups by approximate sequence-length bucket and that can mix requests with slightly different signatures into the same batch. does that impact KV cache semantics?
jia: yes — kernel selection + batch merging can cause different KV cache keys to be created for what used to be identical prefixes if any normalization differs before the batch boundaries. basically we generate per-request probe signature, but then we canonicalize later, so ordering matters.
omar: root cause theory: tokenizer v2 produced different tokenization for some whitespace combos -> different probe tokens -> different prefix hashes. plus unstable serialization for tool fields made many near-duplicates diverge.
kendra: proposal for immediate patch: 1) add explicit tokenizer_version field into cache-signature; 2) canonicalize system prompt by trimming and collapsing multiple spaces; 3) stable-json for tool/function args (sorted keys, deterministic floats formatting); 4) change continuous-batcher to group by signature-hash prefix instead of raw seq bucket to avoid mixing pre/post-normalization.
michael: for validation we need a small perf job: replay 24h of production traffic through a staging runtime with new signing rules and measure hit-rate + p95. also add instrumentation to report examples of mismatched keys (store pair old_key vs new_key sample).
deploy-bot: deploy v2-tokenizer rolled out to prod at 2026-03-15T03:12:08Z (canary->all). :rocket:
natasha: action items: i'll open a small RFC-PR for canonicalization rules. kendra, can you draft the stable-serialize util and a config toggle to include tokenizer_version in signature? jia, can you add extra logs for "cache_mismatch_sample" with both raw inputs + computed canonical key (scrub secrets)?
kendra: yes. I'll push a WIP PR this morning with tests (deterministic JSON ordering + whitespace collapse). we'll default to off behind feature flag.
jia: added quick instrumentation note: include token_count_before/after and seq_hash to help kernel selection debugging.
omar: timeline: patch + canary today, run perf job overnight, roll if hit-rate recovers to within 2% of baseline or fallback to previous tokenizer if not.
michael: small caveat — stable-serialize will add CPU cost on signature creation; microbench shows ~0.5us per request on warm C++ path, acceptable but we should measure at scale. also consider caching the canonicalized signature in request context to avoid double work during batching.
kendra: good call. will add caching for signature in the request struct.
natasha: I'll own the perf job and results dashboard. will include per-route breakdown and a delta table: hit-rate, p95 latency, token cost.
omar: long-term: consider making signature versioned and plumbed through rollout metadata so we can A/B different canonicalization schemes without surprising users.
michael: also let's audit other places we incorporate ephemeral metadata (client library versions, tool names) — they should either be excluded or normalized.
jia: quick troubleshooting tip: to reproduce locally, run:```python tools/replay.py --window 7200 --tokenizer v2 --capture-misses sample.json``` that will dump old vs new signature candidate pairs.
omar: thanks everyone. will track PRs and sign-off on canary. please flag any surprising miss patterns ASAP. :thumbsup:
